title: Very ample on each piece of a finite disjoint union
statement: Let $\Omega$ be a field [def-weil-field] and $Y$ a scheme proper over $\Omega$ [def-weil-proper-morphism], and let $Y=Y_1\amalg\cdots\amalg Y_r$ ($r\geq1$) be a decomposition of $Y$ into pairwise disjoint open and closed subschemes, each $Y_j$ proper over $\Omega$ as a closed subscheme of $Y$. Let $\mathcal M$ be an invertible $\mathcal O_Y$-module [def-sc-invertible-module] such that for every $j$ the restriction $\mathcal M|_{Y_j}$ (the pullback [def-pc-module-pullback] along the inclusion $Y_j\to Y$) is very ample on $Y_j$ in the sense of [def-sc-ample], i.e. the complete linear system of $H^0(Y_j,\mathcal M|_{Y_j})$ gives a closed immersion of $Y_j$ into a projective space over $\Omega$ pulling $\mathcal O(1)$ back to $\mathcal M|_{Y_j}$. Then $\mathcal M$ is very ample on $Y$ in the sense of [def-sc-ample].

source.place: written by an agent for the proof of lem-pc-ample-positive-degree, part (⇐) (no lemma of the Stacks project states it for the complete-linear-system notion of very ample of def-sc-ample; the argument: $H^0(Y,\mathcal M)=\bigoplus_jH^0(Y_j,\mathcal M|_{Y_j})$, and the morphism $Y\to\mathbf P(H^0(Y,\mathcal M)^\vee)$ restricts on $Y_j$ to the closed immersion of $Y_j$ followed by the inclusion of the linear subspace $\mathbf P(H^0(Y_j,\mathcal M|_{Y_j})^\vee)$; these subspaces are pairwise disjoint)

proof.text: *Reading of [def-sc-ample], used alike for the hypothesis on each $Y_j$ and for the conclusion on $Y$.* For a nonempty scheme $X$ proper over a field $k$ and an invertible $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal L$, '$\mathcal L$ is very ample' means: $V=H^0(X,\mathcal L)$ is finite-dimensional, and for some basis $(s_b)_{b\in B}$ of $V$ ($B$ a finite nonempty set, $|B|=N+1$) the sections generate $\mathcal L$, i.e. $X=\bigcup_bX_{s_b}$ with $X_s=\{x:\ s_x\notin\mathfrak m_x\mathcal L_x\}$, and the morphism $\iota:X\to\mathbf P^N_k=\operatorname{Proj}(k[x_b:b\in B])$ [def-pc-proj] attached to $(\mathcal L,(s_b))$ by [lem-weil-pbc-sections-morphism-to-proj-polynomial-ring] (with $A=k$ and $g$ the structure morphism; it satisfies (i) $q\circ\iota=g$, (ii) $\iota^{-1}(D_+(x_b))=X_{s_b}$, (iii) on $D_+(x_b)$ it induces the $k$-algebra map $x_c/x_b\mapsto s_c/s_b$, (iv) $\iota^*\mathcal O(1)\cong\mathcal L$) is a closed immersion. This is the morphism $X\to\mathbf P(H^0(X,\mathcal L)^\vee)\cong\mathbf P^N_k$ of the complete linear system of [def-sc-ample] written in the coordinates of the basis (indexing the coordinates by $B$ instead of $\{0,\dots,N\}$ is a choice of bijection). The steps below use only properties (ii) and (iii) of the morphisms involved, so they hold for every morphism the lemma attaches. If $X=\emptyset$, then $H^0=0$, the complete linear system is the empty projective space and $\mathcal L$ is very ample trivially; so empty pieces $Y_j$ may be discarded (they change neither $Y$ nor $H^0(Y,\mathcal M)$), and if $Y=\emptyset$ there is nothing to prove. From now on every $Y_j$ is nonempty.

proof.text: *Global sections over the decomposition.* Write $i_j:Y_j\to Y$ for the inclusions and $\mathcal M_j=\mathcal M|_{Y_j}=i_j^*\mathcal M$. By [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-module-pullback-restriction], $i_j^*\mathcal M$ is isomorphic, compatibly with restriction maps, to the restriction $V\mapsto\mathcal M(V)$ ($V\subseteq Y_j$ open); we identify the two, so $\Gamma(V,\mathcal M_j)=\mathcal M(V)$, $\mathcal M_{j,y}=\mathcal M_y$ and $\mathcal O_{Y_j,y}=\mathcal O_{Y,y}$ for $y\in Y_j$. The $Y_j$ are open, pairwise disjoint and cover $Y$, so the sheaf axiom of $\mathcal M$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] for this covering (the agreement conditions on $Y_j\cap Y_k=\emptyset$, $j\neq k$, are vacuous) says that $\Gamma(Y,\mathcal M)\to\prod_j\mathcal M(Y_j)$, $s\mapsto(s|_{Y_j})_j$, is bijective; it is $\Omega$-linear. Hence $H^0(Y,\mathcal M)=\bigoplus_jH^0(Y_j,\mathcal M_j)$. By the hypothesis read as in step 1, choose for every $j$ a basis $(s_{j,a})_{a\in B_j}$ of $H^0(Y_j,\mathcal M_j)$ ($B_j$ finite nonempty) with $Y_j=\bigcup_a(Y_j)_{s_{j,a}}$ and a closed immersion $\varphi_j:Y_j\to P_j=\operatorname{Proj}(\Omega[x_{j,a}:a\in B_j])$ with properties (i)–(iv) of [lem-weil-pbc-sections-morphism-to-proj-polynomial-ring]. Put $B=\coprod_jB_j$, and for $b=(j,a)\in B$ let $s_b\in\Gamma(Y,\mathcal M)$ be the section with $s_b|_{Y_j}=s_{j,a}$ and $s_b|_{Y_k}=0$ for $k\neq j$. Then $(s_b)_{b\in B}$ is a basis of $H^0(Y,\mathcal M)$ (the union of the bases of the summands).

proof.text:
*The nonvanishing loci and the quotients $s_c/s_b$.* Let $b=(j,a)\in B$. For $y\in Y_k$ with $k
eq j$, $s_b$ vanishes on the open neighbourhood $Y_k$ of $y$, so $(s_b)_y=0\in\mathfrak m_y\mathcal M_y$; for $y\in Y_j$, $(s_b)_y=(s_{j,a})_y$ in $\mathcal M_y=\mathcal M_{j,y}$ (step 2). Hence $Y_{s_b}=(Y_j)_{s_{j,a}}\subseteq Y_j$, and since $Y_j= igcup_{a}(Y_j)_{s_{j,a}}$ for every $j$, $Y= igcup_{b\in B}Y_{s_b}$: the $s_b$ generate $\mathcal M$. For $c=(k,a')\in B$, on the open $Y_{s_b}\subseteq Y_j$ we have $s_c|_{Y_{s_b}}=s_{j,a'}|_{Y_{s_b}}$ if $k=j$ and $s_c|_{Y_{s_b}}=0$ if $k
eq j$; by the uniqueness of quotients in [lem-weil-pbc-nonvanishing-section-trivializes], $s_c/s_b=s_{j,a'}/s_{j,a}$ in $\Gamma(Y_{s_b},\mathcal O_Y)$ if $k=j$, and $s_c/s_b=0$ if $k
eq j$. (This is the source's 'the image of $Y_j$ lies in the linear subspace $\mathbf P(H^0(Y_j,\mathcal M_j)^\vee)$, and these subspaces are pairwise disjoint', in coordinates: the coordinates outside the block $B_j$ vanish on $Y_j$.)

source.place: proof of lem-pc-ample-positive-degree, part (⇐), the reduction of very ampleness on $X_{\bar k}$ to its connected components; argument written by an agent (the item's source field)

proof.text: *The morphism of the complete linear system of $\mathcal M$.* Let $P=\operatorname{Proj}(\Omega[x_b:b\in B])=\mathbf P^N_\Omega$, $N+1=|B|=\dim_\Omega H^0(Y,\mathcal M)$. By step 3 the hypothesis of [lem-weil-pbc-sections-morphism-to-proj-polynomial-ring] holds for $(\mathcal M,(s_b)_{b\in B})$ with $A=\Omega$ and $g$ the structure morphism of $Y$; let $\iota:Y\to P$ be a morphism it attaches, with (i)–(iv). By step 1 (reading of [def-sc-ample]) it remains to show that $\iota$ is a closed immersion.

source.place: proof of lem-pc-ample-positive-degree, part (⇐), the reduction of very ampleness on $X_{\bar k}$ to its connected components; argument written by an agent (the item's source field)

proof.text: *Surjectivity on each standard chart.* By [lem-weil-pbc-proj-polynomial-twist-chart] the opens $U_b=D_+(x_b)=\operatorname{Spec}(R_b)$, $R_b=\Omega[x_c:c\in B]_{(x_b)}$, $b\in B$, are affine and cover $P$, and $R_b$ is generated as an $\Omega$-algebra by the $x_c/x_b$, $c\in B$; likewise in $P_j$ the opens $U'_{a}=D_+(x_{j,a})=\operatorname{Spec}(R'_{a})$ are affine and $R'_{a}$ is generated by the $x_{j,a'}/x_{j,a}$, $a'\in B_j$. Fix $b=(j,a)$. By (ii) for $\iota$, step 3, and (ii) for $\varphi_j$: $\iota^{-1}(U_b)=Y_{s_b}=(Y_j)_{s_{j,a}}=\varphi_j^{-1}(U'_a)$. Since $\varphi_j$ is a closed immersion and $U'_a$ is affine, [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-affine-cover-criterion] (1) gives that $Y_{s_b}$ is affine and that $\varphi^\sharp_{j,U'_a}:R'_a\to\Gamma(Y_{s_b},\mathcal O_{Y_j})=\Gamma(Y_{s_b},\mathcal O_Y)$ is surjective; by (iii) for $\varphi_j$ it is the $\Omega$-algebra map with $x_{j,a'}/x_{j,a}\mapsto s_{j,a'}/s_{j,a}$, so $\Gamma(Y_{s_b},\mathcal O_Y)$ is generated as an $\Omega$-algebra by the $s_{j,a'}/s_{j,a}$, $a'\in B_j$. By (iii) for $\iota$, $\iota^\sharp_{U_b}:R_b\to\Gamma(Y_{s_b},\mathcal O_Y)$ is the $\Omega$-algebra map with $x_c/x_b\mapsto s_c/s_b$, which by step 3 is $s_{j,a'}/s_{j,a}$ for $c=(j,a')$ (and $0$ for $c\notin B_j$). Its image is an $\Omega$-subalgebra containing a set of generators, so $\iota^\sharp_{U_b}$ is surjective, and $\iota^{-1}(U_b)$ is affine.

source.place: proof of lem-pc-ample-positive-degree, part (⇐), the reduction of very ampleness on $X_{\bar k}$ to its connected components; argument written by an agent (the item's source field)

proof.text: *Conclusion.* The $U_b$, $b\in B$, form a covering of $P$ by affine opens with $\iota^{-1}(U_b)$ affine and $\iota^\sharp_{U_b}$ surjective for every $b$ (step 5), so $\iota$ is a closed immersion by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-affine-cover-criterion] (2). By (iv), $\iota^*\mathcal O(1)\cong\mathcal M$, and $\iota$ is the morphism of the complete linear system of $\mathcal M$ in the basis $(s_b)$ (step 4); so $\mathcal M$ is very ample on $Y$ in the sense of [def-sc-ample] (step 1).
